specification: Implement a cost-bounded cache with per-entry expiry and least-recently-used eviction in the package ttlcache. ttlcache/policy.py defines the class Entry(value, expires_at, cost) with those three attributes, check_ttl(ttl), compute_expiry(now, ttl, default_ttl) and is_expired(entry, now); ttlcache/store.py defines the class Cache; ttlcache/__init__.py exports Cache, Entry, compute_expiry and is_expired (and lists exactly these four names in __all__). policy rules. check_ttl(ttl): None is valid; any other value must be an int or float that is not a bool (otherwise TypeError) and must be finite and greater than zero (otherwise ValueError). compute_expiry(now, ttl, default_ttl): the ttl in effect is default_ttl when ttl is None and ttl otherwise; the ttl in effect is validated with check_ttl; the result is None when no ttl is in effect (the entry never expires) and now + ttl otherwise. is_expired(entry, now): True exactly when entry.expires_at is not None and now >= entry.expires_at, so an entry whose expiry time equals now is already expired. Cache(capacity, clock, default_ttl=None). capacity must be an int that is not a bool (TypeError otherwise) and at least 1 (ValueError otherwise); clock must be callable (TypeError otherwise) and returns the current time as a number; default_ttl is validated with check_ttl. The constructor does not call the clock. Capacity is measured in cost units: every entry has an integer cost of at least 1, and the total cost of the stored entries never exceeds the capacity. Every public method other than the constructor (put, get, peek, delete, keys, total_cost, __len__, __contains__) calls clock() exactly once, as its very first action and also when it later fails on argument validation. An entry that is_expired for the time returned by that call is expired; the other entries are live. Expired entries do not appear in any result (get, peek, delete, keys, total_cost, len, `in`), do not count toward the capacity or the total cost, and are never reported as evicted. A call that raises one of the errors specified above (the TypeError and ValueError cases for invalid arguments, including an unhashable key) leaves the cache exactly as it was before the call, which includes expired entries: they are neither removed nor otherwise touched. The behavior when a key's own __eq__ or __hash__ method raises, or when the clock raises, is unspecified. put(key, value, ttl=None, cost=1) stores the value and returns the list of keys evicted to make room, in eviction order. Validation happens in this order: cost must be an int that is not a bool (TypeError) and at least 1 (ValueError); cost greater than the capacity is a ValueError; then the ttl in effect is validated as in compute_expiry; then the key must be hashable (TypeError). A key that is not hashable raises TypeError in get, peek, delete and `in` as well. The new entry expires at now + the ttl in effect (never when there is none); the ttl of an earlier entry with the same key is not inherited. A live entry with the same key is replaced by the new one and is never reported as evicted. After a successful put the cache holds the new entry, which is the most recently used one, together with the largest group of the most recently used live entries of other keys whose total cost, added to the new cost, does not exceed the capacity; every other live entry of another key is evicted, and put returns the keys of the evicted entries, least recently used first. get(key, default=None) returns the value of the live entry for key and makes it the most recently used, or default when there is none. peek(key, default=None) does the same without changing recency. delete(key) removes the live entry and returns True, or returns False when there is none. keys() returns the keys of live entries as a new list, least recently used first. total_cost() is the sum of the costs of the live entries. len(cache) is the number of live entries, and `key in cache` tests for a live entry; neither changes recency.
